source: NCERT Class VIII, Social and Political Life III, Polity Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Invoking Fundamental Rights
points: Marginalised groups use the **Constitution's Fundamental Rights** to demand justice and equality.
**Untouchability is abolished** (Article 17); **no discrimination** on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or birthplace.
**Cultural and educational rights** (Articles 29–30) protect minorities' language, script and culture.

sections.heading: 2. Laws for the Marginalised
points: **Reservation policy** — a certain percentage of seats in **education, government jobs and legislatures** are reserved for **SCs, STs and OBCs**.
The **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989** — protects Dalits and Adivasis from violence, humiliation and injustice.
The **Manual Scavenging (Prohibition) Act** ended the degrading practice of manual scavenging.

sections.heading: 3. Confronting Marginalisation in Practice
points: Marginalised communities and social movements **organise, protest and use the law** to claim their rights.
Example: the struggles of **Dalits (Dr Ambedkar's legacy)** and Adivasis for dignity, land and temple/well access.
Government schemes and welfare programmes aim to improve their condition, but **implementation** remains a challenge.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Article 17 abolishes untouchability; Articles 29–30 protect minority culture/education.
Reservation for SC/ST/OBC in education, jobs, legislatures.
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 protects Dalits & Adivasis.
Manual Scavenging (Prohibition) Act ended manual scavenging.
Marginalised groups confront marginalisation via rights, law, protest and movements.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Untouchability is abolished by Article 17** of the Constitution.
**Reservation** applies to **education, jobs and legislatures** for SC/ST/OBC.
The **SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act** is of **1989**.
Rights exist in law, but the challenge lies in **implementation**.
